confounder.rationale: Emphysema may have prognostic relevance because pulmonary disease can affect outcomes, but the evidence needed to classify it as a confounder is incomplete. Penalized outcome selection showed only one of three nonzero outcome associations, and no penalized treatment-selection results are available. Since the relationship between emphysema and treatment choice is unknown and unmeasured, a common-cause confounding role cannot be retained confidently.
evidence_comments: Penalized treatment main effects: results unavailable, so no direct evidence that emphysema predicts treatment choice.
Penalized outcome main effects: nonzero in only 1 of 3 analyses, providing weak and inconsistent outcome evidence.
Clinical background: pulmonary disease may affect prognosis, but treatment-choice relationship is unknown.

effect_modifier.rationale: The available effect-heterogeneity evidence agrees across multiple analyses and supports using emphysema to predict differences in treatment benefit. Validation R-loss gains and causal-forest permutation increases are positive in all three overlapping analyses, and penalized treatment interactions are nonzero in all three. Interaction p-values are mostly nominally significant, although the magnitude of improvement is modest and adjusted multiplicity-control information is unavailable. Because validation R-loss directly evaluates treatment-effect prediction, these positive probability-scale results support the modifier role despite the log-odds interaction scale used in some interaction tests.
evidence_comments: Penalized treatment interactions: nonzero interaction group in 3 of 3 analyses.
Univariable R-learner: validation R-loss gains positive in 3 of 3 analyses, with gains of 0.003 to 0.006.
Causal forest: permutation R-loss increases positive in 3 of 3 analyses, with increases of 0.002 to 0.004.
Univariable interaction: p-values of 0.03, 0.06, and 0.04; 2 of 3 are nominally significant, but adjusted q-values are unavailable.
